The services we staff

A carer who is brilliant on a dementia unit may not be the right person for a young man with autism living in his own flat. So we ask about the people you support before we send anyone.

Care and nursing homes

Residential, nursing and dementia care. Nurses for nights, senior carers, healthcare assistants.

Supported living

Learning disability, autism and complex needs. Support workers, sleep-ins and waking nights.

Mental health

Wards, rehabilitation units and community services. RMNs and mental health support staff.

How a booking works

  1. You call or send the form

    Tell us the role, the dates and the type of service.

  2. We agree the terms

    If you're new to us, we agree rates in writing first. The law requires it, and it means no surprises on the invoice.

  3. We find the person

    We contact workers who live close enough and have done this kind of work before.

  4. You hear back

    With a name and a start time (confirmed in writing), or with an honest update if the shift is proving difficult.

When you call, we'll ask you

  • Which role you need, and how many
  • What kind of service it is, and who the person will support
  • The dates and shift times
  • Any skills they must have, such as hoist use, PEG feeding or positive behaviour support
  • The postcode, and who they should report to on arrival

What care managers tell us about agencies

"Nobody picks up at 6am"

Our staffing line is answered at any hour, including weekends and bank holidays, by someone who can actually book a worker.

"They sent someone who'd never done this work"

We ask about your residents or tenants before we choose who to send, and we look for people who have done that kind of work before.

"I couldn't find the paperwork"

Right to work, criminal record checks, references and training are all done before we offer anyone work. If an inspector asks, you can ask us.

How we check the people we send

You remain responsible for everyone working in your service, so you should be able to see how they were checked.

  • Right to work
  • Enhanced DBS, PVG or AccessNI, depending on the nation
  • Two references
  • An interview
  • Mandatory training, with dates
  • NMC check for every nurse

Looking for care work?

Agency work suits people who want a say in when they work: around children, studies or another job. You register once, then accept the shifts that suit you and turn down the rest.

  • Healthcare assistant, support worker, senior carer and nurse roles
  • Shifts offered close to where you live
  • Paid weekly
  • Mandatory training and Basic Life Support at no cost to you
Register with us The roles we recruit

We will never ask you for money. UK law does not allow employment agencies to charge people for finding them work, and that includes visa sponsorship. If someone asks you to pay in our name, don't, and email info@aviteushealthcare.co.uk.

Questions we get asked

How quickly can you get someone to us?

It depends on the role, the time and where you are. A healthcare assistant in a well-connected town is far easier to find at short notice than an RMN in a rural area. Ring as early as you can, and we'll tell you honestly how it's looking.

What does agency staff cost?

The hourly rate depends on the role, the time of day, the day of the week and how much notice you give. Nights, weekends and bank holidays cost more. We agree the rates with you in writing before anyone works a shift.

Do we need to sign anything first?

Yes, a short client agreement. An agency has to agree terms with you in writing before it supplies staff. Once it's in place, you can book one shift or a hundred.

Where do you cover?

We supply care services across the UK from our office in Harrow. Give us your postcode and we'll tell you who we have nearby.

Can we have the same workers each time?

Yes, whenever they're free. Block booking is the most reliable way to keep the same people.

Short of staff this week?

Ring the staffing line, or send a request and we'll call you back.
